I build things to see how they work underneath. Right now that means mechanistic interpretability of small language models: reading a transformer's residual stream with the model's own weights, and watching how it keeps, revises and reuses what it has read.

I also run my own infrastructure. This page is served from a hardened NixOS workstation at home that runs a Bitcoin node, a Lightning node and the Nostr relay this page is assembled from — every block you are reading, the stylesheet included, is a signed event on that relay.

Computer Science (software engineering specialist) at the University of Toronto Scarborough; the [courses](#courses) are listed below. Before the language models: security, browsers, and a long trail of one-page experiments ([everything else](#archive)).

September 2026. Studying how transformers remember: a zero-parameter dictionary built from a model's own write directions (the paper below), continuation lenses that run a model's remaining blocks on an intermediate state, and the attention heads that carry a revised fact to the output.

Keeping the box alive: channels, backups, and the relay behind this page.

tags: How this page works — a block of ronishbhatt.com
drafts.content:
No CMS, no build step, no stylesheet file. This HTML is an empty shell: a few hundred lines of JavaScript and five self-hosted libraries ([preact](https://preactjs.com) + [htm](https://github.com/developit/htm), [marked](https://marked.js.org), [DOMPurify](https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify), [nostr-tools](https://github.com/nbd-wtf/nostr-tools)). Everything else — the header, this text, the cards, the CSS — is a Nostr event signed by this site's key.

At deploy the page is pre-rendered from those events, so it paints before any script runs. Then the browser hydrates it, asks [my relay](https://relay.ronishbhatt.com) first and three public relays as backups, verifies every signature, keeps the newest version of each block, and stays subscribed: when I edit something, every open tab updates. The crypto library loads after first paint; the editor only after I unlock.

The blocks are ordinary long-form notes (kind 30023), so they open in any Nostr client — the ⌁ next to each heading is the same event on njump. The chat is NIP-17: your browser mints a key, wraps the message to mine, and my relay stores it. Unlocking with the site key turns this page into its own editor and opens the console for the box that serves it.

tags: Plant a Thought — a block of ronishbhatt.com
A 7-million-parameter language model trained from scratch, running entirely in your browser. Plant a phrase into its memory, watch it surface in the story, take it out again.
drafts.content: Bip is a word-level GPT (6 layers, 256-wide, an 8,192-word vocabulary) trained from scratch on TinyStories in 444 seconds on one A100, quantised to int8 and inlined into the page: 9.5 MB, no server. Planting never touches the weights. The phrase is run through the model on its own, and the keys and values its attention wrote are spliced into Bip's memory ahead of the story, so every later word can look at them. Taking a thought out deletes those entries again. Story length is a dial on the page.
